settings.name_in_paper: dynamic pricing with limited supply (regret w.r.t. fixed-price benchmark)
unmapped: Actions are posted prices p in [0,1]; feedback is the binary sale indicator (v_t >= p)
Limited supply: k identical items (B = k), n agents (T = n), k <= n; selling stops when supply exhausted; learner knows k
Valuations i.i.d. from unknown demand distribution F with support in [0,1]
Regret is against the best fixed-price strategy A_k^n(p) (expected revenue difference)
settings.definition_quote: A seller has $k$ items she can sell to a set of $n$ agents ... The private values are independently drawn from the same {\em demand distribution} $F$ ... $\Regret(\A) \triangleq \max_p \Payoff[\A_k^n(p)] - \Payoff(\A)$.

settings.name_in_paper: dynamic pricing with limited supply (regret w.r.t. offline benchmark)
unmapped: Posted prices in [0,1], binary sale feedback, k items (B) and n agents (T); learner knows k
Comparator is the offline benchmark: the optimal (Myerson) offline mechanism knowing the demand distribution
settings.definition_quote: Our main benchmark is the maximal expected revenue of an offline mechanism that is allowed to use the demand distribution; henceforth, we will call it \emph{offline benchmark}.

conditions: holds for every demand distribution with support in [0,1]

source.label: lm:UCBcap
source.quote: $\UCBcap$ with parameter $\delta = k^{-1/3}\, (\log n)^{2/3}$ achieves regret $O(k \log n)^{2/3}$.

results.notes: B = k items, T = n agents. Regret is the fixed-price benchmark minus expected revenue (expected-revenue comparison, recorded as pseudo_regret). Same as the upper bound of Theorem 1.2.

conditions: demand distribution is regular (twice differentiable F, concave revenue function)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: There exists a detail-free pricing strategy such that for any regular demand distribution its expected revenue is at least the offline benchmark minus $O((k \log n)^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Comparator is the optimal offline (Myerson) mechanism; mapped to best_policy. Follows from Lemma 4.3 plus Yan's O(sqrt k) benchmark comparison.

symbols.c_F: distribution-dependent constant, c_F = 1 + 1/g'(s_F) with g(s) = s S^{-1}(s)
symbols.s_F: distribution-dependent positive constant; s_F = 1/4 for MHR distributions

source.label: thm:improved-regret
source.quote: For any regular demand distribution $F$ there exist positive constants $s_F$ and $c_F$ such that $\UCBcap$ with parameter $\delta = k^{-1/2}\,\log(n)$ achieves regret $O(c_F\,\sqrt{k}\log n)$ whenever $\fkn\leq s_F$. For monotone hazard rate distributions we can take $s_F = \tfrac{1}{4}$.

symbols.s_F: distribution-dependent positive constant; 1/4 for MHR distributions

source.label: thm:MHR-intro
source.quote: There exists a detail-free pricing strategy whose expected revenue, for any regular demand distribution $F$, is at least the offline benchmark minus $O(c_F\, \sqrt{k} \log n)$ whenever $\fkn\leq s_F$, where $c_F$ and $s_F$ are positive constants that depend on $F$. For monotone hazard rate distributions one can take $s_F = \tfrac14$.

results.notes: Offline benchmark comparator mapped to best_policy.

source.label: thm:improved-regret-trade-off
source.quote: For each $\gamma\in [\tfrac13, \tfrac12]$, consider pricing strategy $\UCBcap$ with parameter $\delta = \tilde{O}(k^{-\gamma})$. This pricing strategy achieves regret $\tilde{O}(k^{1-\gamma}) (1+1/g'(\fkn))$ if the demand distribution is regular and $g'(\fkn)>0$, and regret $\tilde{O}(k^{2\gamma})$ for arbitrary demand distributions.

source.label: thm:improved-regret-trade-off
source.quote: ... and regret $\tilde{O}(k^{2\gamma})$ for arbitrary demand distributions.

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: (a) No detail-free pricing strategy can achieve regret $o(k^{2/3})$ for arbitrarily large $k,n$.

results.notes: Stated as impossibility of o(k^{2/3}); recorded as Omega(k^{2/3}). Proved by reduction to Kleinberg-Leighton unlimited-supply lower bound.

bound.regime: for any gamma_lb < 1/2; arbitrarily large k, n

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: (b) For any $\gamma<\tfrac12$, no detail-free pricing strategy can achieve regret $O(c_F\, k^\gamma)$ for all demand distributions $F$ and arbitrarily large $k,n$, where the constant $c_F$ can depend on $F$.

results.notes: Statement is that no O(c_F k^gamma) bound with gamma<1/2 holds for all F; this is a negation of an upper bound, approximated as an Omega expression. Same as Theorem 1.5.

conditions: demand distribution has monotone hazard rate (MHR)
tuning: delta = ((1/k) log k)^{1/4} (Lemma 7.3 uses delta = (log k log(1/eps) loglog(1/eps)/k)^{1/4})

source.label: thm:descending
source.quote: For some parameters $\epsilon$ and $\delta$, Mechanism~\ref{alg:pp} achieves regret $O\left({k^{3/4}\poly\log(k)} \right) $ with respect to the offline benchmark, for any demand distribution that satisfies the monotone hazard rate condition.

results.notes: Polylog in k only (no dependence on n); recorded as O_tilde. Same as Theorem 1.6.
